paper.title_en: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
paper.abstract_en: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $ρ_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_ρ$ ebits per pair. We show that this cost is robust under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. For every $R>S(A|B)_ρ$, a single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on $ρ_{AB}$ and $R$, merges every weakly almost i.i.d. source along $ρ_{AB}$ with vanishing error. The net entanglement cost is at most $nR$ ebits for all sufficiently large blocklengths $n$. This guarantee also covers the Wasserstein and Mazzola--Sutter--Renner subclasses. Each class contains the exact i.i.d. source, so $S(A|B)_ρ$ is optimal for universal merging within each class. More generally, the same protocols achieve vanishing error whenever the two-pair marginal of the permutation-averaged source converges in trace norm to $ρ_{AB}^{\otimes 2}$.
